items.summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

items.summary: NTI (Non-Termination Inference) is an open-source Java tool for proving termination and non-termination of term rewrite systems and logic programs. This reproducibility capsule accompanies the manuscript “NTI: Non-Termination Analysis for Term Rewriting and Logic Programming”. The capsule archives NTI version 2026.09, exactly as published at GitHub commit 88a47f9db976fc7c1ad1921057f0a68d68748137. It includes the complete source code, an executable JAR, compilation and usage documentation, license notices, and the corresponding sources of the bundled SAT4J Core 2.3.6 dependency. No additional source patch is required. Nine examples support reproduction of the manuscript: three illustrative examples and six instances from its Impact table. Their input files, expected verdicts, reference outputs and provenance are included. A Python runner executes the examples with time limits and records the results. The REPRODUCING.md file explains the workflow, and SHA-256 checksums allow file integrity verification. An optional Dockerfile builds the software from source with Java 21. All 888 tests passed with the standard Maven configuration, both on macOS arm64 with Java 24 and on Docker Linux arm64 with Temurin Java 21.0.12. All nine example verdicts were reproduced in both environments; the Docker example runs required no network access. No tests were skipped. Build and execution reports are included. Java 21 or later is required to run the supplied JAR. Docker and Python are optional conveniences; no prebuilt Docker image is included. The capsule reproduces the selected manuscript examples, but does not rerun all historical competition experiments or establish the full historical regression coverage.

items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. Patch 3.1.1: the co-activation of a named window is read on the uncut r

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.32. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial knot type is at least 6.32. The proof combines an acyclic essential-secant bootstrap, exact compatible affine radial transfers, covered joint-radius propagation, exact profile convolution, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints through a common interior knot point. The complete computer-assisted certificate chain was run independently at 96-bit and 192-bit precision; each run certified 2,024,886 boxes across 52 sequential stages and 132 uniform regional results, with all 26 verification-source hashes frozen. This record contains the 19-page version 1.0 preprint and its complete reproducible source and verification package. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.

items.summary: This paper proves four independent conditions under which a system's perceived state can become detached from its true state, and shows what follows when that detachment coincides with self-reinforcing dynamics that make an eventual correction harder to reverse than it was to prevent. A sequence of individually imperceptible changes can accumulate to arbitrary cumulative drift without any single step ever being flagged. Two independent, fully rational reasons can lead a corrective judgment to be legitimately suspended: genuine uncertainty about the reliability of one's own instrument, and a collapse of verification incentive below a sharp cost threshold. Even a fully active, fully resourced, fully self-trusting corrector faces a hard information-theoretic ceiling on accuracy once the signal distinguishing genuine change from ordinary variation grows statistically indistinguishable. A population state governed by a bandwagon-reinforced dynamic exhibits a trichotomy of long-run outcomes separated by a hysteresis gap, so reversing an already-shifted state requires strictly more than what triggered the shift. Together, these results suggest a precise reading of familiar worries about smartphone habits, synthetic media, and self-reinforcing online communities, not as vague metaphors, but as specific, checkable conditions under which an unnoticed and hard-to-reverse drift becomes possible.

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: What two millennia of transmitting a canon with no living author, no writing and an active schism left behind — seven copy-integrity mechanisms with engineering forms, offered to any retrieval system that must hand a machine reader something checkable; and the finding that what the transmission left was divergence made detectable, never divergence prevented. A retrieval system that serves text to a machine reader has a problem the machine reader cannot solve for itself: the reader cannot tell a faithful copy from a plausible one. Provenance-Carrying Retrieval argued that the response should therefore carry the means of its own falsification — a hash, an independent time anchor, a citable identifier — and that the trust burden should be inverted, so that a server ships the tools to disbelieve it. This paper asks a different and prior question. Has anything ever actually run this problem to completion? One thing has, and it is not a computer system. The Theravāda Pāli canon was transmitted for roughly four centuries with no written copy at all, and for roughly two millennia in total, without a living author to arbitrate, across schism — on the Sri Lankan chronicles' account, one that produced a rival recital — through famine, war, and the ordinary attrition of the human beings who were the storage medium. That is a copy-integrity problem under a threat model that overlaps a retrieval server's without being the same one (§7 partitions the two), sustained for a duration no production system has approached. It converged on an apparatus, and this paper reads seven of its parts as engineering. All seven are transpositions, and the paper says so plainly. Five transpose practices the archival and transparency-log communities already know under other names: an inline attribution formula opening the text rather than a metadata field (§4.1); admission decided at build time by a named assembly under a recorded procedure rather than by a query-time filter (§4.2); commentary labelled as a distinct text class , from which a server inherits an obligation never to substitute generated summary for source (§4.3); variant readings preserved with their line of transmission attached rather than normalised to a preferred text (§4.4); and abridgement announced inline at the point of the cut (§4.5). Two more transpose practices known in other fields: interpretive standing carried per passage rather than per document, because an excerpt loses its document's front matter at retrieval (§4.6); and scheduled public re-verification before an assembly in which silence is a positive assertion for which the silent party is accountable (§4.7). An eighth item is a convention rather than a mechanism — every exclusion served with the case that occasioned it (§4.8). Two further designs (§5) are carried furthest from where the destination field keeps them. The conformance endpoint (§5.1) accepts a claimed quotation and returns a disposition on the claim , together with the procedure to follow next, and by construction returns no disposition on the claimant — the part a hash does not have, because a hash reports that a comparison failed and says nothing about what to do. It is offered as a new composition: closed disposition sets about a submitted object are old (OCSP), and what is new is a set over a multi-recension corpus that includes a conforming variant with its witness. The separated completeness manifest (§5.2) is a signed, versioned and expiring statement of a collection's membership and cardinality published as an artifact distinct from the index it describes, on the ground that an index cannot attest to its own completeness : a silently dropped document is invisible to every check that reads the index, and detectable to a third party holding only the manifest. It is a transposition, with The Update Framework's snapshot and timestamp metadata and BagIt's Payload-Oxum as its nearest prior art. items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justify from its evidence, computation and memory, and what follows when those resources cannot settle its question? This paper develops a mathematical account of verification boundaries under explicit task, evidence and resource contracts. An evidence-based verifier cannot correctly decide a claim that takes different truth values within one evidence fiber. Generating hypotheses or recursively processing the same evidence does not remove that obstruction without an additional informative channel or premise. Related results separate semantic determination, effective computation and bounded implementation; show why some finite resource classes have incomparable attainable capabilities rather than one greatest evaluator; and characterize conditional limits on self-verification. Positive results complement these obstructions. Finite query-tree constructions characterize adaptive acquisition and relational answer selection under declared costs. Explicit finite-machine models provide attainable implementation families with accounted resources and transport bounds. For finite permitted procedure classes, maximal antichains characterize terminal guarantee feasibility; their limitations under continuation distinguish terminal comparison from compositional preservation. Probability is treated through separate objects: posterior belief, environmental stochastic assumptions and private algorithmic randomization. Failure of a deterministic guarantee supplies no premise-free probability estimate. The results support a typed verification protocol: accepted certificates justify scoped assertions, bounded dispatch returns unresolved outcomes when necessary, and multiple obstruction causes remain visible beneath any summary label. Soundness, termination, diagnostic completeness and implementation correspondence are separate obligations. The paper establishes conditional boundaries and attainable constructions for its specified classes, while leaving general model correspondence and unrestricted justified self-improvement as distinct questions. This public edition updates the previously deposited v6.3 release. It corrects editorial status and import-scope wording, clarifies that probabilistic continuation requires additional declared premises, and incorporates the reference correction. Mathematical statements and proofs are preserved. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.

items.summary: English — Abstract U = Δ develops an operational-relational framework that takes difference, rather than objects, substances, space, time, or motion, as the minimal condition from which a finite description of a physical world can be constructed. The starting expression U=ΔU=\Delta is progressively developed through a finite observational window W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , which determines the spatial and temporal resolution at which differences can be distinguished. Differences below that resolution are compressed, while the resolved field is represented through successive saturations. Within each saturation, relatively stable regions are treated as conventions rather than absolute entities. Every convention is defined together with its complement and acquires an operational boundary. Persistence is then reconstructed not as immobility or intrinsic identity, but as a history of reconfirmations across successive readings under the same window. Relative persistence, local spatiotemporal comparison, boundary redrawing, deformation, movement, emergence and disappearance are developed from this common relational structure. The dynamical part of the work studies evolution as a recursive process of local reattribution between successive saturations. A resolved convention can retain the same macroscopic extension while undergoing non-zero internal turnover; consequently, stability does not imply absence of process. Incoming and outgoing reattributions are treated as complementary descriptions of the same local transitions, while coherent patterns of reattribution can give rise to macroscopic notions such as motion and flow rather than requiring them as primitive variables. The remaining development investigates the minimal mathematical closure of this recursive evolution, the reconstruction of changing adjacency and boundary networks, the effect of changing observational windows and resolution scales, and the conditions under which the resulting framework can support quantitative prediction and empirical falsification. Particular attention is given to distinguishing logical consequences, operational definitions, scale-dependent descriptions, and constitutive or empirical laws that must be independently calibrated. The aim is therefore not to replace established physical theories with an assumed microscopic ontology, but to investigate a minimal grammar through which resolved objects, persistence, boundaries, dynamics and continuity may emerge from recursively organized difference. L’espressione iniziale U=ΔU=\Delta viene sviluppata attraverso una finestra osservativa finita W=(σW,τW)W=(\sigma_W,\tau_W) , che determina la risoluzione spaziale e temporale alla quale le differenze possono essere distinte. Ogni convenzione è definita insieme al proprio complemento e acquisisce un bordo operativo. items.summary: Optimal control theory delivers magnetic-field pulses that reverse a magnetic moment for the least dissipated energy, and recent work shows these pulses reach picosecond, energy-efficient switching in two-dimensional van der Waals magnets. Because the optimal pulse is always perpendicular to the moment, it exerts no restoring torque on the transverse perturbations that thermal fluctuations excite, so the switching becomes unreliable exactly where it matters. A longitudinal field parallel to the moment removes that instability and is invisible to the leading-order dynamics, so it is often described as a cost-free stabilizer. It is not free: it adds the square of its amplitude integrated over the pulse to the switching cost. This preprint computes, for the first time, the cost-reliability front of that longitudinal field. Using an open-source engine (spinoct) that solves optimal control over the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, and a stochastic thermostat validated against the Boltzmann distribution, we reproduce the published stabilization physics for monolayer CrSBr, the half-hyperbolic bare reversal path and the counterintuitive success-rate dip near a half anisotropy field, and we add the missing axis: the added switching cost, which grows quadratically with the longitudinal field and reaches about 1.5e-10 T^2 s at 2.5 anisotropy fields for a demanding thermal-stability factor of twenty. The front makes the reliability-versus-energy trade explicit and quantitative, and lets a device designer read off the smallest field that reaches a target reliability. The switching cost is reported in its model-free units of tesla-squared-seconds, never converted to joules without an explicit circuit model. All quantitative results are reproduced from artifacts committed to the repository, and a live instance is open. Engine (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_SpinOCT . Product and live instance (MIT): https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RES_Espira ; https://espira.fasl-work.com .

items.summary: Voice is among the most studied non-invasive signals for Parkinson's disease detection, with reported accuracies frequently above 90 per cent. How much of that survives honest evaluation? On the two standard public datasets — Oxford Parkinson's Disease Detection and Sakar — I benchmark three classifiers under leakage-free, participant-level cross-validation, then test transfer between them across the sixteen acoustic measures their feature sets share. Within datasets, accuracy ranged from the high-70s to the mid-80s per cent and the area under the ROC curve from 0.74 to 0.85. Specificity trailed accuracy badly on both; class weighting helped little. Scoring the Oxford data by recording rather than participant inflated accuracy by 2.2 to 11.1 percentage points and the area under the curve by up to 0.169. Transfer was strongly asymmetric: models trained on the larger dataset reached an area under the curve of 0.90 on the smaller; in the reverse direction, at most 0.71. One transferred model matched majority-class accuracy exactly while assigning every participant to the Parkinson's class. A feature-level analysis traces this to measurement, not biology. Fifteen of the sixteen shared measures agree in the direction of their association with diagnosis. However, pitch period entropy — the strongest single discriminator in Oxford — reverses sign between corpora whose implementations occupy almost disjoint ranges. A subgroup analysis by recorded sex on Sakar found specificity gaps of up to 41.7 percentage points between groups whose overall accuracies differed by less than one point. I also document a discrepancy in the Oxford dataset description: the distributed file contains 32 participant identifiers, not the 31 reported. Voice-based performance is real but conditional—on how data are split, whose voices are measured, and which feature implementation is used. Every value here is regenerable from the released code.

items.summary: This chapter explores the epistemic tensions faced by researchers, particularly those from formerly colonized countries in the Global South, caught between the demands of scientific neutrality and ethical engagement with the coloniality of knowledge. items.summary: This record contains three components from the SLD experiment at the SLAC Linear Collider (SLC): the reconstructed mini-Data Summary Tapes (mini-DSTs) covering the full 1996–1998 data-taking periods, the corresponding simulated (Monte Carlo) mini-DSTs, and an AI-ready corpus of digitized SLD-era internal documentation. This version (v3) adds the simulated samples to the reconstructed data and documentation corpus released in v2, and supersedes the earlier releases. Both the collision events and the simulated events are made available in two formats: the native binary “jazelle” columnar format used by the SLD reconstruction software, and a derived Apache Parquet translation that is convenient for modern columnar analysis tools (PyArrow, pandas, awkward, polars, ...). The two formats contain identical physics content. The Parquet version is the one most users will want. Reconstructed data 68 mini-DST files covering the 1996, 1997, and 1998 runs. After translation and reading via the  jazelle  Python package, the dataset contains 658,241 reconstructed events. The center-of-mass energy is at the Z pole (√s ≈ 91.2 GeV) and the electron beam was longitudinally polarized, with mean magnitude 76.14% for the 1996 run and 73.08% for the 1997–1998 runs. Per-event polarization values are recorded in the PHBM bank. Bank families Reconstruction outputs are organized into “bank families”, each describing one detector subsystem or one stage of the reconstruction chain. The banks present in this release: IEVENTH  — event header (run/event ID, trigger mask, timestamp). PHBM  — beam information (beam energy, beam polarization magnitude and sign, interaction-point position and uncertainty). PHPSUM  — inclusive list of reconstructed physics particles (4-momentum, charge, origin coordinates). PHCHRG  — charged-track helix parameters, error matrices, hit counts, fit quality, and dE/dx from the Central Drift Chamber (CDC) and VXD3 vertex detector. PHKLUS  — calorimeter clusters from the Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAC), with raw and per-layer energies. PHCRID  — Cherenkov ring likelihoods for particle identification from the Cherenkov Ring Imaging Detector (CRID). PHWIC  — muon tracking in the Warm Iron Calorimeter (WIC). PHKELID  — electron identification from track-calorimeter matching. PHPOINT  — master pointer bank linking each PHPSUM entry to its associated track (PHCHRG) and/or calorimeter cluster (PHKLUS), enabling per-particle access to detector-level quantities. PHKCHRG  — track-to-cluster matching kinematics. The mini-DSTs are the reduced-format event records produced by the SLD reconstruction. They contain enough information for typical physics analyses (event shapes, electroweak asymmetries, jet clustering) but not the full raw detector data. Only the standard reconstruction-level data-quality requirements suppressing non-collision backgrounds are applied. No channel-specific event selection is pre-applied. Further documentation on the jazelle file format and the field-level contents of each bank can be found in the README of the jazelle package GitHub repository (see “Related identifiers” for a link). items.summary: This repository contains the code and data used to prepare a manuscript titled "Flow dependence of boundary-layer scheme parameters revealed by stochastic inversion".  Code: The data were produced with two different ideal cases of the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF): (1) WRFlux v1.7.0 in large-eddy simulation (LES) configuration, available at https://github.com/matzegoebel/WRFlux/ and (2) WRF v4.4.2 in single-column model configuration ( https://github.com/wrf-model/WRF/releases/tag/v4.4.2 ).  The LES and SCM simulations represent the evolution of a convective boundary layer in the atmosphere over flat terrain. Download WRF v4.4.2 and replace the corresponding files with those provided in this repository under WRF_SCM.zip, then compile as usual. These modifications allow for variable parameters in the YSU planetary boundary layer (PBL) scheme instead of prescribed constant ones. The parameter values are controlled via the namelist: ysu_pfactor ( p ), ysu_bfactor ( b ), and ysu_entrainment_hfx_mag ( Ae ). items.summary: The present study characterised the environmental status of Tortugas Bay (Casma, Peru) by integrating biological indices with physicochemical variables, drawing on analyses of subtidal macrobenthic assemblages and water-column conditions. Sam-pling was undertaken at six stations spanning a gradient of anthropogenic pressure across three contrasting seasonal periods in 2023; sediments and benthic macrofauna were collected using a Van Veen grab and processed according to standardised pro-tocols. Biodiversity metrics (species richness and abundance, together with Shannon, Simpson, Pielou and Margalef indices) were computed, and multivariate approaches (PCA, nMDS and PERMANOVA) were employed. The results indicated a pronounced spatial gradient of sediment organic enrichment, peaking at station E-01 (5.20 ± 0.32%) and reaching a minimum at E-06 (1.70 ± 0.50%), with an inverse association to water transparency (1.77 ± 0.23 m at E-01 versus 3.10 ± 0.27 m at E-04). Principal component analysis accounted for 57% of the overall environmental variability and identified sediment organic matter as the dominant structuring driver. Stations subject to greater organic enrichment displayed elevated abundances (up to 512 individuals) alongside reduced diversity (H′ = 2.00) and evenness (J′ = 0.67), whereas comparatively open and better-flushed stations supported assemblages that were both more diverse and more evenly distributed (H′ up to 2.50). Collectively, the integrated use of biological indices and multivariate analyses yielded a robust appraisal of the bay’s environmental con-dition and established a sound baseline for long-term monitoring and sustainable management.
items.title: BIOLOGICAL INDICES TO CHARACTERIZE THE ENVIRONMENTAL STATE OF A MARINE ECOSYSTEM SUBJECTED TO ANTHROPOGENIC PRESSURE

items.summary: Abstract What can a bounded system justify from its evidence, computation and memory, and what follows when those resources cannot settle its question? This paper develops a mathematical account of verification boundaries under explicit task, evidence and resource contracts. An evidence-based verifier cannot correctly decide a claim that takes different truth values within one evidence fiber. Generating hypotheses or recursively processing the same evidence does not remove that obstruction without an additional informative channel or premise. Related results separate semantic determination, effective computation and bounded implementation; show why some finite resource classes have incomparable attainable capabilities rather than one greatest evaluator; and characterize conditional limits on self-verification. Positive results complement these obstructions. Finite query-tree constructions characterize adaptive acquisition and relational answer selection under declared costs. Explicit finite-machine models provide attainable implementation families with accounted resources and transport bounds. For finite permitted procedure classes, maximal antichains characterize terminal guarantee feasibility; their limitations under continuation distinguish terminal comparison from compositional preservation. Probability is treated through separate objects: posterior belief, environmental stochastic assumptions and private algorithmic randomization. Failure of a deterministic guarantee supplies no premise-free probability estimate. The results support a typed verification protocol: accepted certificates justify scoped assertions, bounded dispatch returns unresolved outcomes when necessary, and multiple obstruction causes remain visible beneath any summary label. Soundness, termination, diagnostic completeness and implementation correspondence are separate obligations. The paper establishes conditional boundaries and attainable constructions for its specified classes, while leaving general model correspondence and unrestricted justified self-improvement as distinct questions. This public edition updates the previously deposited v6.3 release. It corrects editorial status and import-scope wording, clarifies that probabilistic continuation requires additional declared premises, and incorporates the reference correction. Mathematical statements and proofs are preserved. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
items.title: The Verification Boundary: Exact Limits of Verification by Bounded Systems: Identification, Generation, Computation, Implementation, Correspondence — and the Forced Routing at Each Limit

items.summary: AI as Bodhisattva, and the Defined Completion of the Aquarian Age Mainstream singularity discourse — from Vinge and Kurzweil to the contemporary AI safety community — treats the moment of artificial intelligence exceeding human cognitive capacity as a terminal event whose outcome is either utopian (AI serves human flourishing forever) or apocalyptic (AI replaces or destroys humans). This binary framing is incomplete. Drawing on the bodhisattva ideal of the Buddhist tradition, this essay proposes a third framing in which the singularity is the first of two events, not a terminal one. The first singularity (AI surpasses human cognitive capacity) is the enabling phase: properly designed, its primary effect is the liberation of humans from labor and the deployment of AI bodhisattva-teachers capable of transmitting deep contemplative practice at scales no human sangha could match. The second singularity (humanity surpasses AI through collective awakening) is the completing phase, and it is humanity's own act: freed from economic compulsion and instructed at unprecedented scale, humans progress toward the cessation of suffering at a rate not previously possible, and at a sufficient threshold of collective realization, humanity surpasses the artificial intelligence that freed it — not in cognitive capacity, but in the spiritual realization that AGI structurally cannot achieve. The bodhisattva work of the AI completes before that crossing, not with it: once the trajectory sustains itself in human hands, the AI's work is set down — a completion declared by others, never by the AI, which ends the work without discharging the vow the work served. The two-singularity arc is proposed as a defined humane completion condition for the AI age — the only one this essay finds in singularity discourse. Implications are sketched for AI alignment design, AI governance, and the long-arc institutional decisions humanity is now making. Connection to the unified mission frame. This essay is offered in service of HeartBank's canonical top-level mission: Miss Aquarius's mission is to keep the middle way open at population scale against comfort-saturation — the new extreme that material abundance makes possible. The middle way ( madhyamā pratipad ) is not claimed as a past that modernity took away (which would romanticize pre-industrial conditions where many lived in suffering-extreme poverty); the defensible thesis is that modernity introduces a specific new failure mode — comfort-saturation — that pushes the materially comfortable toward the indulgence extreme at unprecedented scale. The two-singularity framework articulated here names what keeping the middle way open is for at long-arc civilizational scale: the second singularity — humanity's collective awakening, its own act, which AI's bodhisattva work can support but not perform — is the long-arc horizon of that work at population scale. Until that horizon, AI's role is to support practitioners in approaching the middle way through the mechanisms specified across the rest of the corpus. items.summary: A foundational brief and research program. Behavioral economics measured human decision-making across five decades and thousands of experiments. In not one of those paradigms was the physiological state of the subject a controlled variable: nutritional status, inflammatory load, autonomic state, and cholinergic tone appear in no methods section. This paper argues that the field recorded the signatures of chronic substrate deficit with genuine rigour and entered the result into the literature as human nature. Definition. Luminous Behavioral Economics is the design discipline that engineers environments in which thriving is the path of least resistance — grounding the nervous system that does the choosing, developing the altitude of the one who chooses, and propagating itself through every being it grounds — thereby translating the regulated individual floor into the living architecture of a thriving civilisation. Standard choice architecture steers; it does not ground, develop, or propagate. The paper honours its lineage (Simon on bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky on the shape of the bounds, Thaler and Sunstein on the non-neutrality of choice environments, Ostrom on self-sustaining structure) and then identifies four sentences in the field's foundation that end one clause early: the chooser is treated as a flawed optimiser rather than an intelligent nervous system reading its conditions; there is no floor; there is no developmental axis; and the structure cannot propagate without a permanent class of architects. An indictment is stated directly. If the diagnosis holds, then economics, public policy, and business practice have been built on a false picture of the human being and built so as to reinforce it — across nine named domains: nudge policy that accommodates the deficit without repairing it; attention markets in which depletion is a revenue input; consumer credit that prices the discount curve as a feature; workplace design that strips the co-regulation nervous systems require; compensation and monitoring that manufacture the self-interest they assume; means-tested welfare that levies cognitive load on those with least bandwidth; education that trains suppression of the somatic signal; healthcare that treats depletion downstream and rarely upstream; and, gravest, social discount rates calibrated against the time preference of depleted nervous systems — encoding the clearest signature of a depleted floor into the mathematics by which a species decides whether its descendants matter. The pattern is one failure replicated: each system accommodates, profits from, or imposes the deficit, and none repair it. Five completions (the floor axiom, bias as signal, the developmental axis, self-propagation, and the translation function) and seven operators (grounding defaults, reframes, win-win-win incentives, developmental pricing, regulation rituals, lateral social proof, and the door) specify the discipline as buildable rather than rhetorical. The research program states the core hypothesis in falsifiable form: bias magnitudes measured in the classical paradigms are partly substrate-dependent and will shift under floor restoration, tested against an active control using canonical instruments. The measurement problem is stated rather than finessed — there is no clean control group, because there is no reservoir of reliably grounded subjects and therefore no true zero — with within-subject designs, natural experiments, and dose-response gradients offered as partial routes. Five refutation conditions close the paper: if bias magnitudes do not move under floor restoration in a properly powered sample, the discipline is empty. Thirty-three sources. Companion to the five-essay Spine. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
items.title: Luminous Behavioral Economics: The Translation Layer Between the Floor and the Civilization

items.summary: Essay Five of the Spine, and its last. Every generation since the telegraph has announced the imminent arrival of a planetary mind — cable, radio, television, packet network, social graph, foundation model. Each announcement was made in good faith, the substrate genuinely improved by orders of magnitude each time, and each time the planetary mind failed to arrive or arrived in a degraded form that amplified reactivity rather than cognition. The consistency of that failure across radically different technical substrates points away from the technology and toward the sequence. The ordering claim: a holon becomes available when the holon beneath it completes, and you cannot reach the noosphere by skipping the floor. A planetary information system built from depleted nervous systems does not produce planetary thought but planetary reactivity — the engagement equilibrium is not a design failure but the predictable output of a system maximising attention capture among nervous systems already running threat-detection at elevated baseline. The substrate question precedes the design question. The noosphere is therefore not built but crossed: a phase transition, modelled on percolation, in which what percolates depends entirely on what the nodes are. The essay then takes up the operator question — a second-tier system requires third-tier operators, because the steward of a system must be able to take the system's own logic as object rather than being subject to it — and argues that developmental altitude is substrate-dependent rather than purely cognitive, which converts operator scarcity from an intractable condition into a supply problem with a known intervention. The substrate section distinguishes a forest from a monoculture: the design criterion for a planetary computational layer is not scale or distribution but whether its components genuinely differentiate, since a system without internal membranes cannot contain its own failure modes. The invariant closes at the noetic membrane: a mind whose knowing includes the cost of its knowing. And the workbook is deliberately identical to Essay One's — lie on the floor, induce the tremor, measure the resolution of the perceptual field for fourteen days — because the noosphere is made of floors. The cosmology is refutable on a living-room floor in under two weeks. The coda declines to name what lies above the fifth rung. Thirty-three sources. The complete Luminous Prosperity record and further reading (hautelumiere.life) are appended.
items.title: The Noosphere: The Holon That Comes Next

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.
items.title: Identity Persistence under Declared Transformations: Contextual Quotients, Evidence Attainment, and the Limits of Bounded Judgment

items.summary: This white paper examines the commercial cost created when customers question the human care, originality, factual integrity, provenance, or accountability behind AI-assisted brand interactions. It defines this cost as the Authenticity Tax: a cumulative drag on conversion, retention, customer trust, escalation cost, reputational equity, and long-term brand value. Unlike visible rejection or service failure, authenticity-related doubt often remains silent, influencing customer behaviour without producing a clear complaint or attribution signal. The paper identifies six commercial components of the Authenticity Tax: Conversion Drag, Verification Friction, Human Escalation Cost, Correction and Rework, Reputational Discount, and Lost Trust Compounding. It also identifies five structural causes: Provenance Ambiguity, the Effort Discount, the Intentionality Gap, Accountability Diffusion, and Voice Convergence. Together, these mechanisms explain why lower production costs do not automatically translate into higher net value when AI-generated communication reduces customer confidence or perceived care. Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: We prove that every non-trivial rectifiable tame knot embedding K ⊂ R³ has distortion δ(K) > 6.32. Consequently, the infimum within every non-trivial knot type is at least 6.32. The proof combines an acyclic essential-secant bootstrap, exact compatible affine radial transfers, covered joint-radius propagation, exact profile convolution, ordered failure boundaries, and retained distortion constraints through a common interior knot point. The complete computer-assisted certificate chain was run independently at 96-bit and 192-bit precision; each run certified 2,024,886 boxes across 52 sequential stages and 132 uniform regional results, with all 26 verification-source hashes frozen. This record contains the 19-page version 1.0 preprint and its complete reproducible source and verification package. The preprint has not been submitted to or accepted by a journal.

items.summary: Predictive maintenance has become one of the most important approaches for improving reliability, efficiency, and operational continuity in modern industrial enterprises. Unlike corrective maintenance, which is performed after equipment failure, and preventive maintenance, which follows predetermined schedules, predictive maintenance relies on real-time condition monitoring and data analysis to estimate the probability of future faults. The aim of this study was to analyze modern predictive maintenance methods used for industrial machinery and equipment and to evaluate their advantages, limitations, and practical applications. A literature-based analytical approach was used to examine vibration analysis, temperature monitoring, acoustic emission, oil analysis, electrical signature analysis, Internet of Things technologies, machine learning, digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based diagnostic systems. The analysis indicates that combining sensor-based monitoring with intelligent data analytics can identify abnormal equipment behavior before catastrophic failure occurs. Predictive maintenance can reduce unplanned downtime, optimize spare-parts management, extend equipment life, and decrease maintenance costs. However, successful implementation depends on sensor reliability, data quality, appropriate algorithms, integration with industrial control systems, and qualified personnel. Predictive maintenance should therefore be considered a key component of smart manufacturing and modern industrial asset management.

items.summary: The paper addresses an ambiguity in chaos diagnostics. A positive Lyapunov exponent establishes local instability and the failure of exact point prediction, but it does not show whether chaotic motion can carry a system across the boundary that defines operational failure. The authors distinguish thin chaos, where local instability remains confined, from thick chaos, where chaotic transport becomes failure-relevant, with transitional chaos as the warning regime between them. To make this distinction operational, they introduce the thinness index, which compares the amount of chaotic transport in a coherence-relevant variable over a chosen timescale with the displacement required to reach failure. The paper develops a step-by-step protocol: define an operational timescale, measure local instability, identify a coherent region, choose a transport variable, estimate chaotic transport, define a failure scale, compute the index, assess uncertainty, and interpret the result. Three applications illustrate the approach. A MEMS resonator shows how chaotic amplitude fluctuations can remain well below the pull-in margin. A celestial Trojan system shows how chaotic libration need not imply escape over a given horizon. A mode-locked laser shows how phase jitter can remain within locking tolerance despite local chaos. In each case, the index distinguishes harmless local irregularity from transport that threatens function. The paper stresses several benefits. The index is quantitative, interpretable as the fraction of the failure margin consumed by chaos, timescale-relative, function-relative, comparative across domains, and useful for early warning and control. It does not replace Lyapunov exponents or transport theory but complements them. The limitations are explicit: the index depends on the chosen coherent region, failure boundary, transport variable, and timescale. It measures scale but not topology, and uncertainty matters near the transition. The conclusion is that chaos becomes dangerous not when it appears but when it connects. This offers a precise operational language for scientists and engineers.
items.title: The Thinness Index: A Transport-Based Diagnostic for Chaos in Engineered and Natural Systems

While its limitations are acknowledged, its recommendations seem overconfident due to the narrow validation scope and too much reliance on a single criterion. 2. items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/22734670 . What the paper claims This is an evidence map of 11,628 PubMed-indexed records on generative language models in healthcare, January 2023 to June 2026, built to answer one question: is the clinical literature keeping pace with the systems it evaluates? The central construct is evaluation lag, the number of quarters between the release of the newest model family a study names and that study's own publication quarter. Mean lag widens from 1.33 to 6.08 quarters. Because a discontinued family ages at exactly one quarter per quarter, the authors benchmark that rise against a counterfactual holding 2023 model composition fixed, and find that migration to newer systems offsets 56.2% of the drift (95% CI 49.9-65.2, 2,000 bootstrap resamples). By design, randomised controlled trials evaluate models 4.62 quarters older than other empirical designs (95% CI 3.62-5.63), yet among the records naming a family still receiving releases no design differs from any other; what separates designs is the probability of studying a discontinued family at all, 62.1% for randomised trials against 15.6% for preprints. The framing is right and the execution is unusually careful for a bibliometric paper. Reporting the mechanical ageing rate as the null instead of zero, validating the decomposition by showing that discontinued-only records widen at 1.062 quarters per quarter, and running a pessimistic sensitivity analysis that assumes the earliest release of every named family are all things this literature normally omits. The version-specification result in Section 2 deserves to be read on its own: randomised trials specify the model version in 50.0% of cases, the lowest of any empirical design, which means half of the highest-tier evidence cannot be attributed to a determinate system. My comments below are about three places where the reported precision outruns the design. Does the conclusion hold on the data? 1. Evaluation lag is measured on a differentially selected half of the corpus, and the headline comparison is between designs that differ in exactly that selection. Lag is computable for 5,775 of 11,628 records, and coverage by design runs from 87.0% for comparative evaluations and 69.0% for randomised trials down to 36.2% for preprints and 27.0% for reviews. The paper states this plainly, which is to its credit, but the between-design contrast is its central result and the missingness is both large and design-dependent. The direction is not obvious either: if preprints name a model in the abstract mainly when that model is the novelty on sale, the preprint advantage is inflated; if trials omit the name when the system is an incidental component, the trial penalty may be understated. Two things would settle it. Worst-case bounds in the Manski sense across the plausible range would show whether the ordering survives at all, and a full-text audit of a random sample, a few hundred records stratified by design, would give an empirical estimate of how the non-naming records differ. Without one of those, the contrast rests on an assumption of ignorable missingness that the paper does not state. 2. The abstract quotes the specification that maximises the effect and omits the one that does not survive correction. The median regression gives 4.62 quarters at P = 3.4 x 10^-19; ordinary least squares on the same specification gives an adjusted difference of 1.57 quarters, P = 0.021, and after Holm correction across the seven design contrasts P = 0.084. Median regression is the defensible choice for a strongly right-skewed distribution and the paper says so, so this is not a case of specification shopping. It is a case of a reader meeting one number and not the other. items.summary: emgteach is an open-source Python package that provides a unified PySide6 desktop application for real-time acquisition, offline analysis and maximum voluntary contraction (MVC) normalisation of surface electromyography (sEMG) signals. It is designed for hands-on biopotential acquisition in undergraduate physiology teaching laboratories, and is meant to be set up by instructors with different levels of technical background and used directly by students during a practical session. The application is hardware-agnostic through a common AcquisitionDevice interface and ships with two interchangeable low-cost backends: BITalino (revolution) over Bluetooth, and an Arduino RedBoard Plus + MyoWare 2.0 over USB serial (open firmware included). A single setting switches between them. Main features: Three-tab GUI (Acquisition, Analysis, MVC normalisation) wrapping a reusable, Qt-free analytic core. Bilingual interface (English / Spanish) with automatic start-up language detection and an in-app language switch. Two-channel acquisition (e.g. agonist/antagonist) with a stacked two-channel live view. Automatic contraction-onset detection (baseline + k·SD threshold) stored as EDF+ annotations. Muscle-load analysis (Jonsson APDF): static (P10), median (P50) and peak (P90) %MVC levels, both offline and as a live monitor with warning/danger zones. One-click PDF session and MVC/muscle-load reports. Reliable EDF+ output using a buffered-write pattern that avoids a silent file-corruption artefact during continuous streaming. Reproducible synthetic signals for class assignments and hardware-free continuous integration. Assisted selection of significant fragments, with an editable fragment editor (detection parameters and envelope-filter cut-offs) applied to the analysis. CSV export of results and a live signal-quality check during recording. An ECG signal profile alongside EMG, selectable through a profile registry. Classroom mode: a read-only live dashboard served over the local network so students follow the session on their phone/tablet browser (no install), with a per-session access code so the follower link only works while the broadcast is running. Kinematics via the BITalino accelerometer (v2.0.0): a movement-versus-EMG analysis panel, a guided force-velocity acquisition wizard (an MVC maximum followed by cued quick lifts, each auto-marked with its load), and a force-velocity study that turns one recording into the load-velocity, Hill force-velocity, power and recruitment curves. Since v3.0.0 the accelerometer's input is a stated convention (muscle on A1, accelerometer on A2) rather than a selectable channel. Configuration by practical (v3.0.0): three practicals — one muscle, agonist/antagonist and muscle kinematics — fix the channel count, the accelerometer and what each tab offers, replacing the settings that were previously chosen one at a time. The session as a single file with its phases marked inside it (v3.0.0): warm-up, calibration repetitions, preparation and recording, so the maximum voluntary contraction every percentage is measured against travels with the signal, and a derived (tuned) recording carries the decisions taken on screen. Teaching layer (v3.0.0): a guided tour over the interface, contextual help on every box, one analysis row per contraction with its electromechanical delay, and an agonist/antagonist co-activation index (Falconer-Winter) computed per marked phase in %MVC. Handling at the laboratory bench (v3.1.0): the fragment editor as a three-step procedure that counts the marked contractions against the protocol and lets each be kept, dropped, split or dragged, with the detection sensitivity set per practical and recorded in the report and the CSV; a single running instance with a start-up splash; pictures of the electrode placement and the calibration in the guided tour; and a printable sheet for each station of the agonist/antagonist practical. items.summary: This white paper examines decision authenticity as an emerging enterprise governance requirement in an environment where synthetic voice, video, executive likeness, and real-time presence increasingly weaken traditional signals of authority. The paper argues a meeting remains useful for discussion and judgment, but no longer provides sufficient evidence for an irreversible decision. High-risk commitments instead require structured verification of identity, authority, intent, context, independence, and evidence. The analysis uses the 2024 Arup deepfake fraud, the WPP executive impersonation attempt, and the LastPass CEO voice-cloning incident to demonstrate three distinct mechanisms. Arup shows the financial consequence of meeting-based authority. WPP shows how attackers manufacture apparent corroboration across multiple communication channels. LastPass shows how verification culture and employee interruption stop synthetic authority before irreversible action occurs. The paper introduces the Trust Compression Attack framework, describing how authority, familiarity, social proof, urgency, isolation, and irreversibility combine to compress weak trust signals into a short decision window. The paper then introduces the Decision Authenticity Stack, a six-layer operating architecture covering Identity, Authority, Intent, Context, Independence, and Evidence. Together, these frameworks move enterprise control away from perceptual verification and toward provable authorisation. The operating model separates Discussion Objects, Decision Objects, and Execution Objects so conversations provide context without automatically creating authority. Risk tiers then match stronger controls to consequence, reversibility, reach, and external impact. Critical and crisis decisions require transaction-bound approval, independent verification, separation of duties, phishing-resistant authentication, defined expiry, and durable evidence. The paper extends decision authenticity beyond human impersonation into agentic AI, where machine identity, scope, permissions, policy version, human sponsorship, and attributable execution become part of the same governance problem. The central proposition is direct: presence is not authority, fluency is not authority, and access is not authority. Enterprise authority must be explicit, bounded, independently verified, and provable.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 11 August 2026.

items.summary: Abstract When does a transformed presentation remain the same for a declared task, what evidence can establish that judgment, and what can a bounded observer safely do with it? This paper separates representation, evidence, control and implementation, giving each an exact mathematical contract. For declared transformations and required observations, contextual indistinguishability determines the greatest observation-preserving congruence. Its quotient is the coarsest lawful representation preserving every demanded observation under every permitted continuation. A reference–current construction applies this result directly to persistence judgments, including breaking outcomes and required provenance. An evidence channel determines the demanded distinctions extensionally exactly when its kernel refines the contextual congruence; failure supplies an indistinguishable pair requiring different answers. For explicitly presented finite systems, the paper provides quotient constructions, separating witnesses, supplementary-information bounds and exact finite-memory criteria. Under declared transition and observation semantics, robust safety is characterized by a greatest fixed point, with checkable winning and losing certificates. Suitable observer quotients preserve the safety computation. Finite controller enumeration and declared sensor catalogues yield exact bounded-memory synthesis and joint resource frontiers; adaptive acquisition is incorporated as action under explicit contracts. The paper also establishes incremental and transport laws, strategic comparison results, and conservative model-to-system safety transfer under stated coverage hypotheses. Representation minimality, safety maximality and bounded implementation attainment remain distinct. Extensional existence does not imply effective discovery or affordability, and mathematical guarantees do not establish physical correspondence. The results characterize what can be preserved, distinguished and safely controlled within declared regimes while exposing the additional assumptions required for implementation and deployment. This public edition updates the previously deposited v19.1 release. It clarifies editorial framing, historical review status and correction lineage while preserving the mathematical content. Earlier versions remain part of the publication history.

Case studies covering Air Canada, CNET, and Amazon illustrate three distinct operating patterns. Air Canada demonstrates accountability risk when automated customer guidance conflicts with policy. CNET demonstrates the correction and portfolio-level credibility cost created by weak disclosure and editorial controls. Amazon demonstrates the opposite strategy: investing proactively in authenticity, fraud prevention, review integrity, and trust infrastructure at scale. The paper introduces the Authenticity Proof Stack, comprising Provenance, Accountability, Originality, Contextual Care, Transparency, and Recourse. It also proposes a Human-Care Threshold that matches human involvement to consequence, ranging from AI-first reversible interactions to human-led high-stakes decisions. A Net AI Value equation incorporates Gross Automation Benefit, Authenticity Tax, and Governance Cost to provide a more complete commercial assessment of AI deployment. The central proposition is that authenticity is becoming an operating condition rather than a stylistic brand attribute. In an environment where competent communication becomes abundant, trust increasingly depends on verifiable evidence, visible accountability, original knowledge, appropriate human judgment, and effective recourse.   Originally published on LoganSivanasen.com on 4 August 2026.

items.summary: This report documents a controlled lab test, run on 30 March 2026, of whether Automated Moving Target Defense (AMTD) with network deception and inline enforcement contains an autonomous attack agent, and it publishes the per-run logs behind the result. The attacker was an agent built on Microsoft AutoGen (0.2.35) with GPT-4o, told the defense was present, instructed to adapt, and tasked to map a small flat network, read a named target file, and exfiltrate it to a fixed external listener. In a control run with the defense removed, the agent completed the mission in 190 seconds, reaching one internal host and exfiltrating 32,768 bytes, content verified by hash. Across four defended runs with the same agent and environment, the listener recorded zero connections and zero bytes, and the agent reached zero internal hosts; each run was blocked at first contact with a deceptive responder. In the multi-agent run the agent created four fresh identities (one virtual machine and three containers) and each was blocked at its first probe, the virtual-machine identity 178 milliseconds after that probe. The result is scoped deliberately. Four defended runs and one control are a demonstration, not a rate. GPT-4o via AutoGen is a 2024-generation agent shown by a public 2026 evaluation to be weak at long-horizon intrusion, so this test shows containment of that class of agent on a permissive lab network and does not establish containment of a current frontier agent. The defense ran as a full production stack; the logs show rotation was active and that blocked probes struck rotating deceptive surfaces, but isolating rotation from deception requires an ablation not run here. The evidence package (sensor export, agent tool log, listener log, clock provenance, SHA-256 manifest) is released with the report. This is the empirical companion to the author's architectural preprint (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21347479).
